learning_outcomes.text: Possess the ability to design, develop, implement, manage and improve products, systems and processes in different industrial fields, using appropriate analytical, computational or experimental techniques.
Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them working in multidisciplinary teams.
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous lifelong learning for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.
Know and apply knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to know, understand and use the principles of applied Statistics.
Understand the nature of random phenomena and the need to establish a measure of the uncertainty associated with them. Solve probability problems.
Analyze data sets using elementary Descriptive Statistics techniques.
Ability to know, understand and use the principles of applied Statistics.
Knowledge of the fundamental tools of Statistical Inference.

syllabus_topics: Measures of centralization and dispersion. Quartiles
Axiomatic definition of Probability. Meaning and calculation.
Theorem of total probabilities. Bayes' Theorem
Expectation and variance of sums of random variables
Chi-squared, Student's t and Snedecor's F Distributions
Types of sampling. Simple random sampling
Sampling distribution of a point estimator
Point estimator of the mean and point estimator of the variance
Confidence interval for the difference of means
Confidence interval for the ratio of variances
Confidence interval for the difference of proportions
teaching_methods: Practical classes using statistical software (Statgraphics, Excel etc.)
assessment_rules: The general evaluation system for the ordinary session is Distributed or Progressive Evaluation (EP). EP consists of two partial written exams (35% and 60%) and workshops (5%). To pass EP, the total score must be 5 or higher, and the last written test score must be 2 or higher. If the last written test score is less than 2, the EP score is calculated with a penalty: (Exam 1 * 0.35 + Exam 2 * 0.60 - 0.5). Students who do not pass EP may take a single global exam covering the entire syllabus, which must be 5 or higher to pass. The extraordinary session is evaluated by a final exam, which must also be 5 or higher to pass, and its score will be the final grade. A 'Not Presented' grade is given if a student does not attend any progressive tests or the global exam.
